correctness.rationale: For all ten subgroups the orbit-barycenter PL model exactly identifies geometric fixed points. The complete original 2,635-face complex was reconstructed independently; for every subgroup the directly enumerated compatible-orbit simplices equal the simplices obtained from invariant original faces. The central half-turn orbit complex has twelve vertices, twenty-two edges, and four triangles. Its four explicitly free edge-triangle pairs collapse to a connected graph with eighteen edges and twelve vertices, hence the wedge of seven circles. Every other proper fixed complex is empty or six discrete points, as proved by the orbit compatibility rule. Eight signed simplicial Lefschetz values agree with the prior character.

value.rationale: The six-board queen complex is a natural threshold example for integral two-torsion in chess-placement topology. Identifying all geometric fixed loci, including a seven-circle wedge for the half-turn, gives equivariant homotopy information not determined by the ambient Moore-space wedge, a rational character, or elementary queen-placement counts. The ten-subgroup classification is a complete exact invariant for this natural finite object, with a reusable explicit orbit-complex and elementary-collapse proof.
